conventions.convention: The rotating chart is x=R(t)ᵀX, with right-handed rotation about the upward e₃ axis, f=2Ω, and relative velocity u. Coriolis acceleration is −f e₃×u on the force side; e₃×u=(−u₂,u₁,0).

The Boussinesq branch uses periodic lifts on T³=R³/(2πZ)³, continuous first time and spatial derivatives of u,b, continuous second spatial derivatives, and continuous first spatial derivatives of π. The coefficients are constant, with N>0 and ν,κ≥0.

Assume Countable Choice for Lebesgue integration; integrate spatially over Q₃=[0,2π]³ first, then in time. E omits constant reference density and has SI units m⁵ s⁻²; multiplying by reference density gives joules.

The linear Boussinesq and one-layer shallow-water systems are separate adopted approximation branches. Periodicity is an idealization; no reduction theorem, approximation-error estimate, or empirical adequacy is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt the following two distinct approximation branches; they are physical-model assumptions and not conclusions derived from mathematics. The linear periodic Boussinesq branch is u_t+f e₃×u+∇π=b e₃+νΔu, ∇·u=0, b_t+N²u₃=κΔb, with the stated classical regularity, constant f, N>0 and ν,κ≥0. The separate shallow-water branch has positive depth, constant reference density, a flat bottom, hydrostatic pressure and depth-independent horizontal velocity.

Under Countable Choice and the stated smooth periodic linear rotating constant-stratification Boussinesq hypotheses, E(t)=½∫Q₃(|u|²+b²/N²) dx satisfies, for every t₀<t₁ in I, E(t₁)−E(t₀)=−∫t₀ᵗ¹∫Q₃(ν|∇u|²+κ|∇b|²/N²) dx dt. E is conserved when ν=κ=0 and nonincreasing when ν,κ≥0.
